craft_notes: Sthāyin: resolve (the first prescription). Sanskrit first: means (restraint), act (cast), mastery, goal — optatives niḥkṣipet/nayet → L4 keeps imperatives soft ('bind/cast/master/lead'), four verbs marching. Rows: row 1 (goal-last — 'middle way' closes as madhyagatāṃ closes). Rupture: semicolon after 'there' — act done, mastery begins. Close: period on arrival. Minimal pass: 'out and in' for prāṇāpāna (breath both ways, singable); zero else. Read aloud: four stresses march (BIND, CAST, MASter, LEAD); it drills. Rejected: 'prana-apana' kept — killed: L4 sings English, Sanskrit stays in the cite; 'until they pierce the middle' — killed: nayet leads, piercing belongs to bodhana.

lines: Bind the breath out and in, and cast the mind there;
master the winds, and lead them to the middle way.
l4.sanskrit_cite: prāṇāpānanirodhena manastatraiva niḥkṣipet / samyag vāyugatiṃ jitvā yāvan madhyagatāṃ nayet

reads_against.argmap: Entry is breath restrained and mind cast exactly there, then led into the middle.
c1_essence: Breath held, mind cast there, winds mastered into the middle — that is entry.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta with vīra-utsāha (wonder braced by resolve)
